question: What is the main purpose of tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: Removing secretions to keep the airway clear

explanation: Suctioning is primarily performed to clear trapped mucus and fluids when a patient cannot cough them out independently. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is suction applied intermittently rather than continuously during airway clearance?

options.A: To allow the suction machine time to build up mechanical pressure
options.B: To make sure the sterile catheter stays clean on the inside
options.C: To prevent severe damage to the airway lining and low oxygen levels
options.D: To give the nurse enough time to measure the suction gauge

explanation: Continuous suctioning pulls too much air out of the lungs and aggressively grips the delicate tissue inside the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: A patient with an endotracheal tube needs suctioning when which sign appears?

options.A: Warm, dry skin with pink nail beds
options.B: Audible or visible secretions in the airway tube
options.C: Deep, quiet breathing sounds in all lung fields
options.D: A normal, steady heart rate and blood pressure

explanation: Seeing or hearing mucus rattling in the tube tells the nurse the airway is partially blocked and needs clearing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which condition is a clear contraindication for routine nasotracheal suctioning?

options.A: Severe bleeding disorders or severe nasal trauma
options.B: Needing a routine check of vital signs every four hours
options.C: A mild low-grade fever without respiratory changes
options.D: Being sleepy but easily waking up when spoken to

explanation: Passing a catheter through a damaged or bleeding nose can cause dangerous hemorrhage and further trauma. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the typical safe suction pressure range for an adult patient?
explanation: Pressures between 80 and 120 mmHg are strong enough to remove thick mucus without causing excessive trauma to the airway lining. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: You are preparing a suction catheter for an adult patient with an artificial airway. What is the rule of thumb for selecting the catheter size?

options.A: It must be the largest possible size that fits through the opening
options.B: It should always be a uniform size 14 French regardless of the tube
options.C: It should fill the entire inside of the tube to grab all the mucus
options.D: It should take up no more than half the inner diameter of the airway

explanation: Leaving enough open space around the catheter prevents a vacuum from forming inside the lungs, which would dangerously drop oxygen levels. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why is a patient hyperoxygenated right before undergoing tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: To force thick mucus plugs to dissolve and loosen up inside the lungs
options.B: To build up an oxygen reserve and prevent dangerous drops during the procedure
options.C: To test if the oxygen tank and flowmeter are working properly
options.D: To help the patient fall into a deep sleep so they feel no discomfort

explanation: Because the suction catheter temporarily removes air from the airway, extra oxygen beforehand protects the patient from sudden hypoxia. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is an important step when preparing a conscious patient for suctioning?

options.A: Explaining what will happen to reduce anxiety and fear
options.B: Administering a strong sleeping pill before starting
options.C: Telling them not to cough under any circumstances
options.D: Asking them to hold their breath until the procedure ends

explanation: Clear communication helps calm the patient, ensuring better cooperation and less panic during a vulnerable moment. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended time for a single suction pass?
explanation: Limiting passes to 10 to 15 seconds prevents the patient from running out of oxygen and developing dangerous heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: When should suction be applied as you insert the catheter into the artificial airway?

options.A: Never apply suction while inserting the catheter
options.B: Apply continuous suction the entire time you push it in
options.C: Apply suction only when the catheter hits the back of the throat
options.D: Apply suction in short bursts on the way down

explanation: Applying suction during insertion damages the delicate lining of the airway and removes helpful air; suction is only applied while withdrawing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why might a patient experience a sudden dangerous drop in heart rate during suctioning?

options.A: A sudden spike in blood pressure from anxiety
options.B: Too much clean air rushing into the stomach
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve in the airway
options.D: An allergic reaction to the sterile glove powder

explanation: The vagus nerve runs close to the airway and triggers a slowing of the heart rate when irritated by the suction catheter. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h6)

question: During suctioning, your patient's oxygen saturation drops rapidly and their heart rate becomes irregular. What is your very first action?

options.A: Document the normal finding and check the patient again in one hour
options.B: Quickly insert the catheter deeper to grab the remaining thick mucus
options.C: Turn up the wall suction pressure to finish the procedure faster
options.D: Stop suctioning immediately and provide oxygen via manual resuscitator

explanation: Safety comes first: stop the trauma, remove the negative pressure, and give the patient oxygen to recover. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which detail is essential to include when charting after suctioning a patient?

options.A: Color, consistency, and amount of the removed secretions
options.B: The exact brand name of the sterile gloves used
options.C: The name of the company that manufactured the suction machine
options.D: The room temperature at the moment of the procedure

explanation: Recording the characteristics of mucus gives vital clues about infection, hydration status, and overall lung health. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the best way to evaluate if the suctioning procedure was successful?

options.A: Ask the doctor to review the nursing notes at the end of the shift
options.B: Measure the weight of the empty suction canister on a scale
options.C: Listen to the patient's lung sounds and check oxygen levels
options.D: Confirm that the patient has fallen asleep comfortably

explanation: Checking lung sounds and oxygen saturation directly shows whether airway clearance improved breathing function. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)
